title: Line Plot Worksheets: Fraction Measurements
intro: Teach fraction line plots by separating the scale from the frequency.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Read one fractional length, then count how many marks appear at that length. Use equivalent fractions when discussing the scale.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Three crosses above 1/2 mean three measurements of half a unit.

The fraction describes each length. The number of crosses describes how many times that length appears. Three crosses do not change the label to three units.

Ask your student

Does this fraction name a length or a number of measurements?

If your student needs help

If the student adds labels instead of counting marks, point to one recorded measurement at a time.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each sheet reuses two total-count questions and two questions about how many measurements have the smallest shown value. Every plot uses 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, and 1, with one through three crosses at each value. All four values appear.
